PPE Training Quiz: Complete the PPE Training Quiz in RSS.

tasks.title: 3.2 — EHS Required Online Trainings

lines.html: Complete all required trainings at the UC Learning Center. Send a screenshot of your Training Transcript page to Wenbo Zhang (wen_zhang@berkeley.edu) when done — this is required before the lab walk-through.

tasks.name: UC Berkeley EH&S courses and transcript

lines.html: Read and sign every SOP relevant to your work before beginning experiments — this is a required part of onboarding. SOPs are available in hard copy in the lab and in the Group SOP folder on shared Drive. Categories include: Cryogens, Acutely Toxic Gases, Acutely Toxic Chemicals, Corrosives, Mutagens, Perchloric Acid, Peroxide Forming Chemicals, Pyrophoric Materials, Strong Oxidizing Agents, Hydrofluoric Acid, Self-Heating Substances, Water Reactive Materials, and Flammable Liquids and Solids.

tasks.title: 3.3 — Chemical Hygiene Plan & SOP Handbook

lines.html: Read the Boettcher Lab Chemical Hygiene Plan in full. Then read and sign every SOP in the lab handbook binder.
Note the physical binder location.
Note where Safety Data Sheets (SDS) are stored for chemicals you will use
Chemical Hygiene Plan: link pending — ask the lab safety officer for the current approved version.

tasks.name: Chemical Hygiene Plan and SOP handbook

lines.html: After completing your EHS trainings (3.2) and sending your transcript to Wenbo, schedule your in-person lab walk-through. Wear PPE when in the lab.
Everyone has work-stop authority. If something looks unsafe, stop and check with your advisor or a senior lab member before proceeding — it is always better to pause than to risk an incident.
The walk-through covers Tan 271, 272, 373, 379, and 383. You will locate every emergency response item, chemical storage area, waste station, and gas shutoff in person. Have the floor map open:
Lab Floor Map
Get the Safety Officer’s signature for this step.
Complete with your trainer. You will be fitted for safety glasses and confirm your lab coat, and learn to select the correct glove for lab chemicals.
Glove guide:
Nitrile (standard): everyday handling of aqueous solutions and most salts
Thicker nitrile or neoprene: concentrated acids and bases
Double-glove: acutely toxic chemicals — Ni, Co, Cr(VI), Pt compounds, V compounds
Butyl rubber gloves: required for Piranha solution (H₂SO₄ / H₂O₂) — nitrile is not adequate
Always check the SDS for any chemical you haven't handled before

⚠️ Piranha solution (H₂SO₄ / H₂O₂) requires specific training before use. Contact Meg Takezawa for training on handling and disposal before working with Piranha. Butyl rubber gloves are mandatory — standard nitrile is not adequate.
NEVER PUT YOUR FACE INSIDE THE FUME HOOD. Keep the sash at or below the marked line at all times; keep your face outside the sash plane
Position materials at least 6 inches from the front edge; no clutter blocking airflow
If the hood alarm sounds: stop work, close sash, notify supervisor immediately
Your trainer will verify airflow and demonstrate correct posture.
Using the lab floor map, physically walk to every emergency response item in the building. Each has a Lord of the Rings code name on white painter's tape. Enter code names as your answers.
Items: Class ABC fire extinguisher · Sand bucket · Fire alarm · Eye wash station + shower · Chemical spill kit · First aid kit · AED · Calgonate Gel (HF spills)
→ Open Emergency Response Quest
Before you begin a new experiment, you MUST complete the Boettcher Lab Risk Assessment Form with your mentor. The form covers hazards, likelihood and severity ratings, and contingency plans.
Complete a risk assessment each time you do something new that carries a hazard of injury -- not just your first time. Post the completes form in Slack #risk-assessments
Any experiment scoring above 15 (Extreme risk) requires Shannon’s signature before it begins.
→ Open Risk Assessment Form
If working with cryogens at UC Berkeley, complete EHS 109 — Cryogens Safety in the UC Learning Center before this work. Verify facility-specific requirements with your supervisor.
If working with compressed gases at UC Berkeley, complete EHS 111 — Compressed Gas Safety in the UC Learning Center before this work.

Contact Meg Takezawa for specific training and approval before handling or disposing of Piranha solution. Follow the current SOP, hazard assessment, and chemical-specific glove compatibility guidance.

Chemical labeling: Every container must be labeled with your initials, the date, and the contents — described in enough detail that a stranger could identify the substance without guessing. Unlabeled chemicals result in heavy fines and costly disposal. We have had many instances of forgotten unknown chemicals. No exceptions.
Lost and found: If you find something lying around the lab, put it in the lost and found. It is cleared after each group clean-up — anything unclaimed by then is gone.

Group cleanup takes place every other Friday in Tan 2 and Tan 3 (campus members). If you have a specific task that you would like to help with, inform Sree and Martha in advance. Otherwise, they will assign you a task. All group members must be present for the entire group clean up.

tasks.title: 3.8 — Chemical Inventory Quest

lines.html: RSS inventory: All UCB lab members must add new chemicals promptly when they arrive and delete containers as soon as emptied.

Log in to the RSS Chemical Inventory App at app.riskandsafety.com using your @berkeley.edu email. Download the mobile app for barcode scanning (iOS · Android). See also the EHS RSS Inventory Tutorial. If the lab inventory doesn't appear, email Matthew Zoerb (matthew.zoerb@berkeley.edu) to be added to the roster.
You can also browse the Lab Chemical Inventory Spreadsheet (link pending) to familiarize yourself with what's on the shelves.
The quest has two parts:
Part A — App tasks: Search a chemical and read its hazards · Add a test container · Delete the test container. Show each step to your trainer live.
Part B — Scavenger hunt: Find each chemical storage location; each has a Pokémon code name on white tape.
→ Open Chemical Inventory Quest (link pending)

tasks.name: UC Berkeley chemical inventory (RSS) and quest

lines.html: LBNL members use the Chemical Management System (CMS) instead of the UCB RSS inventory quest. Confirm the required inventory orientation and access with your LBNL supervisor.
Waste handling requirements are covered in the Waste Disposal Quest (3.9) and during your lab walk-through (3.4). Detailed compliance rules are covered in EHS 105.

For full guidance on labeling, storage, accumulation limits, pickup requests, and waste categories (chemical, sharps, universal waste), read the UCB Hazardous Waste Management Fact Sheet. Use app.ehs.berkeley.edu/hwp to create waste labels and submit pickup requests.

tasks.title: 3.9 — Waste Disposal Quest

lines.html: Proper waste disposal is a legal requirement. First declare your expected waste streams, then find all waste containers. Create EH&S waste tags whenever a container approaches capacity — don't wait until it's full.

Common waste streams in this lab: aqueous heavy metals (Ni, Co, Cu, Fe, Cr, V, Ba) · platinum group metals (recoverable — separate stream) · strong acids · strong bases · strong oxidizers · non-halogenated flammable solvents · halogenated solvents · contaminated solids / wipes · sharps and broken glass
Each waste location has a code name on white tape. When a container is full, label it before EH&S pickup:
→ Create an EH&S Waste Label
→ Open Waste Disposal Quest (link pending)

tasks.name: Waste Disposal Quest and EH&S labels

lines.html: Before generating or disposing of waste at LBNL, receive facility-specific waste segregation, labeling, accumulation, and pickup instructions from your LBNL supervisor or EHS contact. Campus EH&S waste labeling procedures do not automatically apply at LBNL.
Read the full Boettcher Lab Potentiostat Etiquette Guide before using any potentiostat. Key rules:

Reserve channels on the lab Google Calendar (boettcherlab gmail) — include your name, potentiostat name, and channel(s). [GRAD/POSTDOC] Mentors must be named in the reservation; mentees cannot book independently.
If you haven't started within 30 minutes of your booking, the channel is open to anyone.
Max 3 Biologic channels per person at once; max 100 hours back-to-back.
For long experiments (100+ hrs) not requiring continuous EIS, use a Squidstat or other power supply first — not a Biologic.
After a 100-hour block, you may not rebook that channel for 3 days.
Conflicts → speak to the people involved first. If unresolved, contact the current Potentiostat Governor.
Your trainer will walk through cell assembly, electrode handling, electrolyte degassing, gas line use, and emergency shutdown.
For B30 equipment at Chu Hall (SEM, XPS, major instruments), ask Yang for access to the equipment lists and ensure you are added to the relevant WPCs before training.
Add instrument-specific training here as your project develops. Each new instrument requires sign-off from the responsible lab member before independent use.

The two most common gas suppliers for UC Berkeley labs are Airgas and Linde-Praxair — both deliver directly to the lab. See the Airgas ordering instructions for how to place an order. Ask Yang for the correct speedtype before ordering.
The Bakar NanoEngineeering Center (BNC) has shared equipment including SEM, metal deposition tools, and more. Access requires separate training and registration.

intro.html: Now that you know how to be safe, it is equally important to know how to be a good lab citizen. This phase covers lab norms and housekeeping, then walks you through the signed safety training steps required before independent work.
Read the Group Philosophy Guide before your first week. It covers Shannon's expectations on research culture, work-life balance, communication, safety, and what it means to be a good lab member.
